title: Use fewer borders
principle: Refactoring UI public tip: borders are a heavy default. Prefer box shadow, contrasting background regions, or simply more space. Question every border—does it earn its visual cost? Partial, hairline borders beat cages.
procedure: Inventory all borders on the view.
For each, try in order: more space, background contrast, soft shadow, then hairline if still needed.
Prefer separating list rows with padding over full-width rules.
When a border stays, make it subtle (light grey, thin, maybe partial).
Re-check with remove-ai-tells: cages and card grids are slop fingerprints.
examplePrompts:
Border diet (Refactoring UI):
- List every border/divider.
- Replace with spacing or background contrast where possible.
- Keep at most hairline separators for true section breaks.
- No double-boxed cards inside bordered sections.
Return a kill-list of removed borders.
This settings page is a stack of outlined boxes. Flatten: one surface, spacing for groups, hairline only between major sections.
Border diet second pass on screenshots only: circle every remaining box outline. Keep at most one hairline system; delete the rest for space or background tint.
promptWhy: Flattening nested boxes attacks a frequent AI layout tell.
Screenshot circling makes residual cages visible to a critic.
tips: Use fewer borders—official Refactoring UI marketing/public tip.
Accent borders can add color without painting whole surfaces (public tip family).
This desk uses hairline rules and double rules sparingly as letterpress, not cages.
Accent borders can introduce brand color without painting whole fills (public Refactoring UI tip family).

workedExamples.title: Card cage stack
workedExamples.before: Every widget in a 1px border on a bordered panel.
workedExamples.after: Panel background only; widgets separated by 16–24px; one hairline above footer actions.
workedExamples.body: Public tip: try shadow, contrasting backgrounds, or space instead of borders.

workedExamples.title: List without rules
workedExamples.body: Row padding alone often separates items cleaner than dividers—especially on paper/ink UIs.

workedExamples.title: When borders stay
workedExamples.body: Inputs on white-on-white may need a subtle edge or soft fill; make it one intentional treatment, not a unique border per control.

workedExamples.title: Quiet Folio hairlines
workedExamples.body: This desk uses double rules and hairlines as letterpress punctuation—not a cage around every card.

antiPatterns: Heavy black rules competing with type.
Replacing every deleted border with a heavy shadow (still noise).
checklist: Spacing/background tried before keeping a border.
Accent border if any is intentional and sparse.

stateRequirements.responsive: Check 390px and desktop plus 200% zoom; preserve reading order, wrap long text and keep actions reachable.
stateRequirements.accessibility: Use semantic headings and native controls, visible labels and focus; normal text contrast at least 4.5:1.
stateRequirements.keyboard: Complete the primary action using Tab, Shift+Tab, Enter and Space; no pointer-only information or focus trap.
stateRequirements.reducedMotion: Remove nonessential movement; preserve all state and information without waiting for animation.
stateRequirements.loading: Show pending feedback only during real work; retain context and allow navigation away.
stateRequirements.empty: Distinguish no content from no matching results; explain how to proceed or reset filters.
stateRequirements.error: Explain the failed action, retain user input and offer recovery; never claim success on failure.
stateRequirements.interruption: A newer action wins; cancel or ignore stale results and keep controls responsive.
stateRequirements.stateChange: Announce important results politely without moving focus unexpectedly.

compatibility.rule: Start with one technique. Add at most one companion for a distinct unsolved problem; candidates are suggestions, not verified compatibility.
conflicts: Two techniques changing the same visual role require an explicit winner.
Do not combine multiple entrance or attention effects on one target.
Aesthetic subtraction must not remove semantics, feedback or attribution.
compatibility.stop: Stop when the named task is clearer and acceptance evidence is recorded; do not add polish without a problem.
